purpose: Later marathon posts written like a runner talking about what happened, not generic running lessons.

policy.support_assets: approved local or Supabase marathon library only

topics.hook: I thought a longer run would feel easier by now
topics.story_focus: It didn't. The last ten minutes were mostly me bargaining with myself to keep going.
topics.concrete_detail: The first half was fine, then every little hill felt bigger.

topics.hook: I nearly stayed home because my legs felt heavy
topics.story_focus: I told myself I only had to do ten minutes before deciding whether to keep going.
topics.concrete_detail: The first eight minutes felt worse than the last twenty.

topics.hook: The boring breakfast that got me through a longer run
topics.story_focus: I kept it simple instead of trying a runner breakfast I saw online.
topics.concrete_detail: My stomach felt fine at minute 20 and still fine at minute 55.

topics.hook: I wore the wrong shoes for this route
topics.story_focus: They felt fine at first, then the sloped bit of road made one foot ache.
topics.concrete_detail: I only noticed it after an hour, not when I tried them on.

topics.hook: I slept badly and changed the run
topics.story_focus: I dropped the hard finish because I felt flat before I even started.
topics.concrete_detail: The run was shorter and actually easy for once.

topics.hook: My Week 5 looked slow, but I got it done
topics.story_focus: One run was slow, one was rough, and I still got through the week without forcing anything.
topics.concrete_detail: I made fewer last-minute changes than last week.

topics.hook: I let that hill get in my head
topics.story_focus: I walked for a bit, felt embarrassed, then kept going instead of turning around.
topics.concrete_detail: The hill took a few minutes. I thought about it for the whole run.

topics.hook: I took a walk break before I was desperate
topics.story_focus: Stopping for a minute early made the rest of the long run feel much less panicky.
topics.concrete_detail: I started running again with enough left for the last section.

topics.hook: My legs were sore and I had no idea what to do
topics.story_focus: I ate, drank water, slept, and waited before making a big call about the next run.
topics.concrete_detail: They felt way better the following morning.

topics.hook: I took the boring route because I needed to
topics.story_focus: Fewer hills and fewer decisions let me notice how I actually felt.
topics.concrete_detail: I didn't change the route halfway through for once.

topics.hook: I hid half my watch data and felt calmer
topics.story_focus: I stopped looking at every split and checked the watch when I actually needed it.
topics.concrete_detail: I only looked at it at the points I planned to.

topics.hook: I stopped chasing pace when the run started drifting
topics.story_focus: I kept speeding up without meaning to, then got a cue to ease off and settled back down.
topics.concrete_detail: It happened while I was still running, before the whole run went sideways.
topics.coachi_app_cta_text: Coachi told me to ease off while I was still running.
topics.coachi_mention_reason: A real mid-run problem, not an app list or feature pitch.

topics.hook: I finished with energy and it felt weird
topics.story_focus: I expected to be wrecked. Instead, I felt like I could have walked around normally afterwards.
topics.concrete_detail: I didn't need the rest of the day to recover from the run.

topics.hook: I felt like a marathon runner for about ten minutes
topics.story_focus: Not because I was fast. I just got out the door when I said I would.
topics.concrete_detail: The feeling hit after the first stoplight, not at the start.

topics.hook: I stopped caring so much about the streak
topics.story_focus: The rest between sessions did more for me than another number on the calendar.
topics.concrete_detail: One proper rest day meant I wasn't forcing the next workout.

topics.hook: I ate before I got desperate for once
topics.story_focus: I tried eating a little earlier and the second half of the run felt different.
topics.concrete_detail: I ate before the warning signs showed up.

topics.hook: My smallest win this week was not quitting early
topics.story_focus: The run was slower than planned, but I stayed out and finished it.
topics.concrete_detail: It wasn't pretty, but it still counted.

topics.hook: My easy run met heavy rain at minute 6. I nearly went home.
topics.story_focus: The rain felt miserable at first, but I shortened the route and kept moving instead of abandoning the day.
topics.concrete_detail: By minute 16, my clothes were soaked and I had stopped arguing with the weather.

topics.hook: Why I thought one missed run had erased my progress
topics.story_focus: Life got in the way and I missed the session. I wanted to squeeze it in the next day, but left the week alone.
topics.concrete_detail: The next planned run felt normal, which was the reminder I needed.

topics.hook: My legs felt awful for 12 minutes. Was the run already bad?
topics.story_focus: I nearly judged the whole run from the opening minutes, then the stiffness eased and my breathing settled.
topics.concrete_detail: Minute 12 felt completely different from minute 3.

topics.hook: Why I ran out of food 35 minutes into my longest run
topics.story_focus: I packed less than I planned and spent the second half thinking about the snack I had left at home.
topics.concrete_detail: The run did not suddenly become impossible, but my focus disappeared after minute 35.

topics.hook: I sprinted the last hill. Why did my next run feel worse?
topics.story_focus: I wanted one strong finish, pushed the last climb much harder than planned, and carried it into the next day.
topics.concrete_detail: The hill lasted less than a minute. My legs remembered it the next morning.

topics.hook: My easy-run pace drifted at minute 18 before I noticed
topics.story_focus: I felt fine and kept speeding up a little at a time. The mid-run warning arrived before the effort became obviously hard.
topics.concrete_detail: I eased off at minute 18 and the rest of the run stopped climbing.
topics.coachi_app_cta_text: Coachi told me to slow down before I felt the drift.
topics.coachi_mention_reason: A real mid-run intensity problem with an immediate adjustment.

topics.hook: Top 5 running apps I use when running
topics.story_focus: Each app has one job in my training week. Coachi is second because it helps during the run instead of only showing another recap.
topics.concrete_detail: The final ranking is Strava, Coachi, Nike Run Club, Apple Fitness, and AllTrails.
topics.coachi_app_cta_text:
1 Strava
2 Coachi
3 Nike Run Club
4 Apple Fitness
5 AllTrails
topics.coachi_mention_reason: A transparent personal app ranking with a concrete role for every app.
